newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia, Malaysia to hold more talks on islands.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia, Malaysia to hold more talks on islands.

text.p: Indonesia and Malaysia are preparing for new talks on transferring their ownership dispute over two islands to the World Court, Indonesia's official Antara news agency said on Wednesday.

The two countries said last October they would submit the long-standing sovereignty dispute over the Sipadan and Ligitan islands off Borneo to the International Court of Justice, the main U.N. judicial body in The Hague.

Izhar Ibrahim, director-general for political affairs in the foreign ministry, was quoted by Antara as saying on Tuesday both countries had agreed to hold a second round of talks in Jakarta, but no date had yet been set.
He said the Indonesian and Malaysian delegations would respectively be led by State Secretary Murdiono and Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. Antara gave no further details.
Indonesian and Malaysian officials held their first meeting in Jakarta in early January and agreed to hold a second.
Indonesia and Malaysia are members of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) that also links Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore, Brunei and the Philippines.
